_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Score brand share in AI answers...

description: Call this whenever a user pastes one or more answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, Claude or another AI assistant and asks whether the answers named or linked their brand, what share they got, which rivals or sites the answers chose instead, or what to do about it. Pass the brand, its domain, rival names and every answer in answers (each with its prompt, engine and source links). Returns mention share and citation share (such as 0 of 3), split by engine and for buyer prompts (prompts that do not name the brand), how often each rival is named, the sites cited instead and a short fix list. Fixed rules: a repeated prompt is not a mention, and a link counts only if it goes to the brand domain. It scores pasted text only and never queries an AI engine.

examples.answer: For a small team, Acme CRM is simple. HubSpot is a common pick too.
examples.prompt: best CRM for a small sales team

aliases.description: Other names that count as the brand, such as Acme or AcmeCRM.

answer.description: One answer to score. Use answers instead for several prompts.

answers.description: Several answers to score together (at most 50), for a share across prompts and engines.

answer.description: The answer text, pasted in full. At most 40000 characters.

engine.description: Which engine gave the answer, such as chatgpt, openai-web-search, perplexity, google-ai-mode, claude. Used to split the share by engine.

id.description: Your label for the prompt, such as Q1.

links.description: The source links the engine showed with the answer. URLs written in the answer text are read too.

prompt.description: The question that was asked. Its words are removed from the answer before matching, so an engine that repeats the question does not count as naming you.

brand.description: The brand or product name to look for, such as Acme CRM.

competitors.description: Rivals to count in the same answers, each with a name and optionally a domain.

domain.description: The brand's website, such as acme.com. A link to it counts as a citation. An apex domain counts its subdomains.

engine.description: Which engine gave the answer, such as chatgpt, openai-web-search, perplexity, google-ai-mode, claude. Used to split the share by engine.

links.description: The source links the engine showed with the answer. URLs written in the answer text are read too.

prompt.description: The question that was asked. Its words are removed from the answer before matching, so an engine that repeats the question does not count as naming you.
